messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Higher serum vitamin D levels were associated with lower odds of poststroke depression symptoms in acute stroke patients.
Sentence: "In multivariate analyses, the serum levels of vitamin D and interleukin-6 were associated with the development of PSD after adjusted possible variables (OR = 0.976, 95% CI: 0.958-0.994, p = .009; OR = 1.029, 95% CI: 1.003-1.055, p = .027)."
Measured as: poststroke depression (HAMD-17 ≥ 7)
Population: 152 acute stroke patients
Intervention: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower serum vitamin D levels (continuous association)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 152
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Serum vitamin D levels showed no significant association with EPDS-defined postpartum depression (EPDS ≥9).
Sentence: "We defined an EPDS score of ≥9 as being positive for postpartum depression, and serum ketone levels were found to be higher in the group with an EPDS score of ≥9 during the second trimester; however, there were no other significant findings."
Measured as: postpartum depression (EPDS score ≥9)
Population: Pregnant women in Japan followed through pregnancy and postpartum (99 analyzed)
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Women with EPDS <9 vs ≥9
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 126
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
